macro.headline: Bull regime intact on the surface, but momentum and vol are flashing caution.
macro.story:
The headline tape still looks constructive — SPY, QQQ, the Dow, and even the Russell 2000 are all sitting above both their 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and SPY is only -0.6% off its 52-week high. That is, by definition, still a bull regime. But underneath that surface, the picture is meaningfully more tense than the trend label suggests, and our job is to read the conflict honestly rather than airbrush it.

Momentum has rolled over across every major index. SPY's MACD histogram is negative at -4.51 with price below signal, QQQ's MACD histogram is deeply negative at -7.0, and the Nasdaq composite is sitting at RSI 38.7 in oversold-extended Bollinger territory. SPY is down -3.8% over five days and QQQ is down -6.8%. That is a real momentum break, not noise, and it shows up most aggressively in the growth/tech complex. The Dow and Russell are holding up better, which tells you the selling is concentrated where positioning was most crowded.

Volatility is confirming the tension. VIX is at 20.71, up +34% over five days, with MACD above signal and rising — and the VIX3M/VIX ratio has collapsed from contango toward 1.03, meaning short-dated fear is catching up to longer-dated fear. That is the classic stress signature. On top of that, DXY is trending up with RSI 65 and MACD above signal, which is pressuring metals hard — gold is down -12.5% over 21 days and silver -25%, both oversold-extended. The DXY-strength-to-commodity-headwind relationship is validated and currently active.

Net-net: indices are above their SMAs (bullish structural), but MACD is bearish across the board, VIX is spiking above 20, and breadth has narrowed to defensives. Per our framework that combination — price above SMAs but MACD bearish plus VIX spiking plus commodities declining — is exactly the LOW-confidence macro setup. Stance is NEUTRAL because the regime hasn't broken, but conviction to press longs is low until momentum stabilizes.

newsletter:
**[THE SPINE]** Dollar strength bleeding into commodities and metals is the dominant force this week. DXY at 100.1 sitting above both its 21d and 50d SMA with RSI 64.5 is the *** ACTIVE *** macro signal, and it is doing real damage: Gold -12.4% over 21d, Silver -25.3%, Oil -12.0%. Equities are wobbling around it (SPY -1.9% on 21d, BB below_lower, RSI 40.7), but the cleaner, higher-conviction trade running through the tape is the dollar-up / hard-asset-down axis.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The regime is CHOPPY/transitional (confidence 4/10), VIX 21.5 with a +19% pop on the month but still in contango (VIX3M 22.9), and the curve remains positive — so this is not a panic, it is a grinding repricing. The DXY_METALS_TAG signal HOLDS in backtest (corr -0.45 sustained in 70% of rolling windows), and you can see it expressed cleanly in Gold RSI 24.4 / BB below_lower and Silver RSI 27.6. Per our discipline: Gold and Silver are oversold in a trend driven by a rising dollar — not a mean-reversion setup. Same for Oil (RSI 43.6) and TLT (RSI 48.7, BB mid): backtest says no edge fading either, and the 10Y at 4.53% with RSI 56 is no ceiling — that signal DOESN'T HOLD.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is rotating into defensives and dollar-insensitive cash flows: XLV +6.9%/21d (leader), XLP +2.5%, XLF +2.0%, XLRE +0.9% — all leaders. The casualty list is exactly what a strong-dollar tape should produce: QQQ -2.8%, XLK -0.7% despite its ACCELERATING_BULLISH trajectory, and IWM -1.1%. Industry rotation is narrow and barbell: flows are pushing into Consumer Electronics, Software – Infrastructure, and Semis on one end; nothing is formally rotating out, but the FADING themes are unambiguous — Precious Metals & Inflation Hedge complex and Broad Commodity Reflation are both breaking down.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The leadership that has already run is Semiconductors — HOT 13 months and +258%, the largest spell on record with a CEILING flag. That is exits-not-entries territory; do not chase. The in-range, early-innings pockets are Software – Infrastructure (HOT only 1 month, +3% gain, well below the typical +18% run) and Internet Content & Information (HOT 1 month, still slightly red). Healthcare Plans (HOT 2 months, +9%) fits the defensive bid. The cleanest un-run setup on the board is Banks – Regional via PNC (coil 96.8%, LEAN BULLISH flow) — a coiled name in a sideways industry that benefits from a steeper curve and a firm dollar. Caveat on metals: do not try to catch Gold or Silver here — the washout-retest base rate says 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days, so even if a bounce comes, the first low is rarely the last.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** DXY 100.54 resistance is the tripwire. A decisive break above re-accelerates the metals/commodity downtrade and likely keeps QQQ/XLK heavy; a rejection back below the 21d SMA (and toward 98.88 support) is the first real signal the spine is cracking and that Gold/Silver oversold readings can convert from "trend" to "tradeable." Secondary trigger: SPY reclaiming 749.53 resistance would say the equity wobble was noise around the dollar move, not the start of something larger.
